summary: US-023b: Consumers accept performance.published schema 5 before anything emits it
description:
**Second slice of TKT-175.** Pure consumer-side tolerance, shipped **before** any producer change — that ordering is the point of the slice, not an accident of scheduling.

ADR-017 §5b′ requires a consumer to dispatch on `schema` **before** decoding `data`. If catalog began emitting schema 5 while inventory and access still capped at 4, both would park the message and readiness would fall. Shipping the consumers first makes that unreachable, and it is only expressible as a separate merge.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Inventory's and access's `performance.published` consumers accept **schema 5**, dispatching on `schema` before decoding `data`, and ignore the field they do not yet use.
- [ ] The future-schema tripwire fixtures move to **schema 6**, so the "park an unknown future variant" behaviour is still proven rather than accidentally satisfied by the new ceiling.
- [ ] The `schema <= 0` broken-envelope rule still terminates and still does not touch readiness (ADR-017's bottom end).
- [ ] Fixtures are **hand-written envelopes**, not built from the type under test — a fixture built from that type encodes the compatibility it claims to prove (ADR-017; TKT-61 shipped this bug twice).
- [ ] Nothing emits schema 5 yet. Catalog is untouched; the schema-4 golden is byte-identical.

Quality gates: `make check` green; consumer tests; readiness unaffected.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` ... Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

reference.summary: The architecture, every design decision and the full test plan live in TKT-175's kind=plan and kind=plan-final — read those first, they are not repeated here

governingAdrs.why: The whole ticket. Dispatch on schema before decoding data (§5b′); the schema<=0 bottom end is a broken envelope, not the future; a fixture built from the type under test cannot fail. TKT-61 shipped the ordering bug twice past a mutation-checked suite.
Shared durable consumer lifecycle: a parked or terminated message must not silently affect readiness in a way this change alters.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Readiness — PASS

Deliberately the narrowest slice in the chain, and the one whose ORDER matters more than its content. Its value is that it makes the next ticket's producer change safe to deploy.

Shaping is inherited: TKT-175's `kind=plan` (gpt-5.6-sol) and `kind=plan-final` (main-agent) decided the architecture, the design, the test plan and the risks before this ticket existed. This child re-scopes delivery, not thinking.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-180

Second slice of TKT-175. Blocker TKT-179 merged (`7f6f8be7`). Branch `TKT-180-consumers-accept-schema-5` off `origin/main`. Gateless under the standing waiver. Planning inherited from TKT-175's `kind=plan-final`.

**Stop-condition pre-check:** consumer-side only, no migration, no auth, no money, no CI config. Nothing emits schema 5, so the blast radius is a schema ceiling and two fixture numbers.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### Implementation — TKT-180

**Implemented by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**. PR [#150](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/150) · commits `5effa904`, `54bd340b`, `fd430f22`, `d0a3c9b3`.

Shipped: **access** accepts `performance.published` schema 5 (its future-variant fixture moves to 6). **Inventory** does not, and gains a comment at `maxKnownPublicationSchema` saying why.

The ticket began as "both consumers accept schema 5" and ended as "only access does". That inversion, and three rounds of corrections to ADR-041's rollout section, are the substance — see `kind=summary` on ai-review.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial code review — TKT-180

**Reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`**, per `config.models.aiReview`. Cross-model check holds.

**Four passes — the absolute cap.** Every round found the previous round's *rollout advice* still wrong in a way that would have left rule-enabled pools silently unenforced. Findings: **1 → 2 → 2 → 1**, all real, all fixed.

The pattern is worth naming: **every error was in the sequencing, never in the architecture**, and each was invisible until the previous one was fixed.

#### Pass 1 — the ticket's premise was half wrong

**Inventory must not accept schema 5 early.** ✅ Verified: `ProvisionSeated` writes `consumed_events` and short-circuits on replay (`seat_claims.go:129-135`). So a binary that accepts schema 5 while ignoring the orphan flag provisions a pool, records the event, and acks it — and a later capable binary redelivered that event **short-circuits and can never build the projection**. The pool is permanently rule-less and nothing reports it.

Parking is the opposite: loud (readiness latches false), reversible, self-resolving. **"Accept and ignore the field we cannot use" is strictly worse than doing nothing.**

The pass also caught that my schema-5 test *passed for the wrong reason*: `orphan_prevention_enabled` is not in `publicationData`, so the hand-written flag was discarded on decode and the assertion only ever checked schema-4 behaviour. Removed with the arm.

→ Inventory reverted to ceiling 4, tests restored byte-identical, access bump kept.

#### Pass 2 — the fix's *reason* was wrong, and the sequence contradicted itself

- **The general rule.** I wrote that early acceptance is safe when handling is idempotent and unsafe when the consumer records completion. ✅ Verified false: access records `consumed_events` too (`store/policy.go:45`) and is nonetheless safe — because schema 5 changes nothing access owns. The discriminator is **semantic completeness**: *a consumer may accept a variant early only if its handler performs every effect it will ever need from that variant.* As written my rule condemned the access bump this ticket ships and would have authorised irreversible partial handling for being repeatable.
- **A shared merge does not order a deployment.** I argued consumer-first "is only expressible as separate merges" and then put inventory's arm and catalog's emission in one ticket. Catalog and inventory start independently. → catalog's emission carved out as **TKT-183**; TKT-181 narrowed to inventory-only.
- Also corrected: my claim that parking is "self-resolving the moment a capable binary deploys" is **false for inventory** — quarantined originals are acked, so recovery is `reprocess-quarantine` **plus a restart**, by an operator.

#### Pass 3 — the order shipped the producer before the enforcer, and forgot the past

- **181 → 183 → 182 opens a window** where organizers have the rule on, inventory records it, and buyers can still strand seats. TKT-182 is dormant until a schema-5 pool exists, so shipping it first costs nothing. → order is now **181 → 182 → 183**.
- **The sharpest finding of the whole epic.** TKT-179 shipped the setting *before* TKT-183 ships the transport, so a performance can be published against a rule-enabled map **today**: catalog emits schema 4, sets `event_emitted_at`, and **never emits it again** — re-POSTing publish is idempotent. Inventory provisions an ordinary seated pool, and nothing later in the sequence repairs it. Those pools stay permanently rule-less while the back office insists the rule is on.
  → TKT-183 gains a **correction wave** with a fresh event identity (the existing `reemit-policies` ids may already sit in `consumed_events`, where a replay is a silent no-op), and inventory must **upgrade an existing pool** rather than assume it only provisions new ones.

  This is a hazard our *own slicing* created. Splitting a feature into safe increments opened a window the increments themselves must close.

#### Pass 4 — the correction wave races catalog's own rollout

During TKT-183's **own** rolling deployment an old catalog replica can publish schema 4 **after** the scan has passed that performance — permanently unrepairable, same hazard one layer in. → the wave starts only once every schema-4-producing replica has drained, or converges via a watermark or repeated reconciliation, with a deterministic per-performance correction identity.

#### Cap

Stopping at four. The last amendment (`d0a3c9b3`) is **reviewed by no second model**; it is documentation, the gate is green over it, and the verification is mine.

#### Gate

`make check` green after all four commits.

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
### PO validation — TKT-180 (self-validated under the waived Gate 4)

Merged `3159ead8` (squash of PR #150), branch deleted. `make check` re-run on merged `main` → `EXIT=0`.

| AC | Met | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Consumers accept schema 5 before anything emits it | ⚠️ **amended** | **Access** does. **Inventory deliberately does not** — the review proved early acceptance there is irreversible. The AC as written was half wrong and is recorded as such rather than quietly satisfied. |
| Future-schema tripwire still proves something | ✅ | Access's fixture moved to schema 6. Inventory's stayed at 5 and is byte-identical to `main`, which is correct now that its ceiling is unchanged. |
| `schema <= 0` bottom end intact | ✅ | Untouched. |
| Hand-written fixtures | ✅ | The one test that was *not* — it decoded a flag absent from `publicationData` and so only ever asserted schema-4 behaviour — was deleted with the arm it defended. |
| Nothing emits schema 5 | ✅ | Catalog untouched; schema-4 golden byte-identical. |

#### The honest part

**The ticket's premise was half wrong and the review is what found it.** "Consumers accept the new schema first" is textbook ADR-017 and it is exactly right for access. For inventory it is *worse than doing nothing*: `ProvisionSeated` records `consumed_events`, so accepting-and-ignoring makes a pool permanently rule-less and un-repairable, where parking would have been loud and reversible.

Then three more rounds, each finding the previous round's rollout advice still wrong: the general rule I wrote condemned the very bump this ticket ships; the sequence contradicted its own "separate merges" argument; the order shipped the producer before the enforcer; and the correction wave raced catalog's own rollout.

**Every finding was about sequencing. The architecture never moved.**

#### Newly unblocked

**TKT-181** — inventory implements schema 5 and its adjacency projection.
